title: Why Are BATL, TPET, XOM, CVX, USO, UCO Stocks Rising Overnight? - Stocktwits
content: Shares of multiple oil companies and oil exchange-traded funds climbed overnight late Sunday after Brent crude prices rose above $90 a barrel amid escalating tensions between the U.S. and Iran. Mohamed El-Erian, Chief Economic Advisor at Allianz, noted on X late Sunday, “Responding to this weekend's US-Iran escalation, Brent crude is currently above $90 a barrel in Asian trading.” WTI crude futures expiring in August also rose more than 2% to $84.33 per barrel. As a result, oil companies Battalion Oil Corp. (BATL) and Trio Petroleum Corp. (TPET) rose more than 7% and by over 8% in the overnight session. Oil majors Exxon Mobil Corp. (XOM) and Chevron Corp. (CVX) also rose about 1% each. Meanwhile, the United States Oil Fund (USO), which tracks the daily price movements of West Texas Intermediate (WTI), climbed more than 2% at the time of writing, while ProShares Ultra Bloomberg Crude Oil (UCO) rallied more than 3%. The Light, Sweet Crude Oil Futures (CL_F) were also 2% higher. Oil prices soared back up as tensions between the U.S. and Iran escalated over the weekend after the American military launched a ninth consecutive night of attacks on the Middle Eastern country. “CENTCOM began conducting a new wave of strikes against Iran at 7 p.m. ET today for the ninth consecutive night. The strikes will continue degrading Iranian military capabilities used to attack commercial vessels and civilian mariners transiting the Strait of Hormuz,” the U.S. Central Command said in a post on X. Over the weekend, CENTCOM confirmed that a third U.S. service member had died following recent fighting in the Middle East. The military had initially reported two fatalities and one service member missing after an Iranian attack in Jordan on July 17 before later confirming the third death. Meanwhile, Iran Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi condemned the U.S. strike on the under-construction Darquoin power plant, calling it a dangerous attack on Iran's civilian infrastructure. In a post on X, he said the strike made Washington fully responsible for the resulting instability and warned that Iran would take appropriate measures to safeguard its national security and interests. "The longer the Strait remains closed and the war escalates the greater ​the risk that oil prices will have to rise to around $150/barrel to bring demand down to match the hit to supply," Shane Oliver, Head of Investment Strategy and Chief Economist, at AMP reportedly told Reuters, adding that "This is not our base case but it's a high risk again." Meanwhile, Garfield Reynolds, MLIV Asia team leader at Bloomberg, reportedly said the widening spread between Brent crude and WTI reflects growing concerns that an escalation in the U.S.-Iran conflict could disrupt global energy supplies, though the gap remains narrow enough that equity markets have largely shrugged off the risk compared with the early stages of the war. Analyst Patrick De Haan said on X that rising oil prices would likely send gas prices higher in the U.S. in the coming week. “Brent crude oil up ~3% reaching $90/bbl, while WTI crude up ~2% to nearly $85/bbl. RBOB up 5c/gal, national average gas price will hit $4/gal either tomorrow or Tuesday, likely to see increases ahead for most states!” he said. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around BATL stock slipped from ‘extremely bullish’ to ‘bullish’ over 24 hours while it was in the ‘neutral’ territory for TPET. XOM and CVX stocks were trending in the ‘bullish’ territory at the time of writing. Sentiment for USO and UCO stocks, meanwhile, was in the ‘extremely bullish’ and ‘bearish’ territories, respectively. One bullish user on Stocktwits said, “$USO $BATL I'm not selling, no matter what." BATL stock is up more than 46% this year, while TPET has declined nearly 60% in the same time. XOM and CVX have gained more than 20% each in 2026. USO and UCO have surged nearly 80% and 113% year-to-date. For updates and corrections, email newsroom[at]stocktwits[dot]com. Comments posted here will also appear on symbol pages. Advanced Micro Devices appears to have secured, or is close to securing, Claude developer Anthropic as a chip customer, with speculation swirling online after a senior executive referenced the AI startup in code published on GitHub. AMD shares rose 1.3% in the overnight session late Sunday. A YAML code file from an unnamed AMD senior director listed Anthropic as a “customer,” chip news site SemiAnalysis reported on Sunday. SemiAnalysis said Anthropic was assigned the maximum 30 “priority boost points,” placing it alongside existing hyperscale customers such as Meta – fueling speculation that AMD could formally announce a partnership with the AI startup at its flagship Advancing AI conference next week. “Note that Anthropic is still in the evaluation phase, and if AMD doesn’t announce Anthropic at its upcoming Advancing AI conference, that means @AnushElangovan’s FDE team has yet to address all of Anthropic’s concerns regarding software quality, and further improvement will be needed,” SemiAnalysis wrote. Meanwhile, Anthropic has reportedly been hiring engineers with ROCm experience (AMD’s AI software stack), suggesting it is preparing to further diversify its computing infrastructure, Jefferies analyst Blayne Curtis said in a recent note. Anthropic is not a publicly confirmed AMD customer. The AI startup has publicly said it trains and serves Claude using a mix of Nvidia GPUs, Amazon’s Trainium chips, and Google’s TPUs, with Amazon remaining its primary cloud and training partner. The AMD Advancing AI 2026 conference will run over Wednesday and Thursday at the Moscone Center in San Francisco. The company is expected to focus its announcements around AI infrastructure, new silicon-to-software pipelines, and enterprise-tier development. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment for AMD remained ‘bullish,’ unchanged from the previous day, with traders noting speculation that Anthropic is becoming an AMD customer. “The recent market bloodbath just flushed $AMD from its 584 peak to the 490s. Daily RSI is screaming deep oversold in the 29-34 range. This is exactly what an extreme discount looks like,” a trader wrote. “The massive ‘Advancing AI’ event drops July 22-23 with the 2nm Zen 6 and Helios platform. This killer catalyst will likely torch the shorts, triggering a violent rebound off the $478 hard support next week,” they said. AMD stock has declined for three days straight, losing 16%, but remains 132% higher year to date. The chipmaker will report its second-quarter results on Aug. 4. SemiAnalysis said an unnamed AMD senior director posted it, not Vice President Anush Elangovan. AtaiBeckley (ATAI), Palo Alto Networks (PANW) and Travelers Companies (TRV), all reached 52-week highs on Friday as investors moved away from vulnerable areas of the technology sector and toward companies backed by stronger fundamentals, with capital flowing into businesses with clearer growth catalysts, essential services and proven earnings power. Atai Life Sciences and Palo Alto Networks stocks ended the session 0.9% and 1% higher, while Travelers Companies stock climbed 9%. AtaiBeckley stock reached a four-year high of $7.22 on Friday, as its psychedelic medicine business gained momentum after a multibillion-dollar acquisition agreement reshaped investor expectations for the sector. The rally followed Eli Lilly and Co. (LLY )'s July 16 announcement of a deal to acquire AtaiBeckley for $6.75 per share in upfront cash, valued at up to $3.8 billion, including milestone-based payments. The transaction pushed psychedelic treatments closer to mainstream pharmaceutical acceptance as investors viewed the acquisition as a sign of confidence from a major drugmaker. The deal centers on AtaiBeckley’s experimental therapies, including BPL-003 and VLS-01. BPL-003, an intranasal formulation based on 5-MeO-DMT, is being developed for treatment-resistant depression and has received FDA Breakthrough Therapy Designation. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around the stock remained in ‘extremely bullish’ territory. Palo Alto Networks stock touched a record high of $368.80 as investors showed confidence in its cybersecurity business. Demand increased for Palo Alto’s security platforms, including Cortex and XSIAM, as companies prioritized protecting their digital systems from growing AI threats. Capital One upgraded the stock to “Overweight” from “Equalweight” and increased its price target to $421 from $307. The firm expects the cybersecurity company to benefit from growing demand for AI infrastructure, rising cyber threats, a spike in security spending and the need to protect new AI systems. Retail sentiment around the stock remained in ‘bearish’ territory. The Travelers Companies stock also reached a record high of $370.43 after reporting stronger-than-expected fiscal second-quarter results. The insurer posted earnings of $10.04 per share, while revenue reached $12.15 billion, both exceeding the analysts’ consensus estimates of $5.39 and $10.98 billion, respectively, according to Fiscal AI data. Travelers improved its combined ratio to 83.6% from 90.3% last year, showing stronger underwriting performance. Investor sentiment toward the stock remained positive. So far this year, TRV, ATAI, and PANW stocks have gained between 26% and 94%. (ORCL) and SpaceX (SPCX) fell to annual lows last week amid concerns around future growth, mounting debt, and a post-IPO profit-taking scenario. NFLX stock fell more than 7% at close on Friday as investors continued to react negatively to the company’s latest earnings outlook. ORCL declined to a 52-week low before reversing to close up 1.77%. SPCX stock extended two consecutive weeks of losses to close down more than 5%. NFLX stock fell to a yearly low of $65.08, about 45% down from its 12-month high, as the streaming giant’s weaker-than-expected outlook for the third quarter deepened investor concerns about its future growth. The company forecast third-quarter earnings of $0.82 per share on $12.86 billion in revenue, slightly below analysts' expectations. However, during the earnings call, CFO Spencer Neumann said quarterly growth may appear uneven due to tougher comparisons with last year, stressing that Netflix remains focused on full-year performance. He expects third-quarter revenue to rise about 12%, driven by subscriber growth, selective price hikes and expanding advertising revenue. Netflix also narrowed its 2026 revenue guidance to $51 billion to $51.4 billion. Meanwhile, veteran investor Michael Burry said last week that he is on the fence about whether Netflix produces content “that is long-lasting, watchable on repeat, across generations.” Drawing comparisons with peers Disney and Pixar, he said the rivals “produce evergreen content,” raising questions about whether Netflix’s content can generate similar long-term value. NFLX stock is down more than 24% this year even as retail sentiment remains ‘extremely bullish’ on Stocktwits. ORCL stock fell to a 52-week low of $121.50 on Friday, although the company’s shares recovered to close in the green. Oracle has been on the receiving end of criticism for its aggressive spending on cloud infrastructure and rapidly growing debt. The company recently said that it plans to spend up to $95 billion in capital expenditures in fiscal 2027 and raise $40 billion through debt and equity. This has fueled worries about rising leverage and negative free cash flow. Those concerns intensified after S&P Global downgraded Oracle's credit rating to BBB-, citing its reliance on a handful of large customers, including OpenAI. The company has also been weighed down by growing uncertainty around OpenAI's business prospects, raising questions about Oracle's AI-driven growth strategy. ORCL stock is down more than 35% this year. Despite the worries, retail sentiment on Stocktwits was ‘extremely bullish’ at the time of writing as users see the dip as an opportunity. SPCX stock fell to an all-time low of $122.12, dipping further below its IPO price of $135. Elon Musk’s aerospace company, which made its historic debut on Wall Street last month, declined for a sixth-straight session. SpaceX has seen heavy selling following its aggressive capital-raising plans. Meanwhile, last week the company scrubbed the latest launch of its Starship mega rocket due to technical glitches. Musk said in a post on X that the launch was automatically aborted after some of the engines failed to ignite. In a separate post, he said SpaceX plans to replace two Raptor engines before making another launch attempt, which is most likely to take place early next week. The test flight was intended to mark the debut of an upgraded version of Starship designed to support future Starlink deployments and NASA's lunar missions. According to a Reuters report, SpaceX is now targeting July 23 for its next launch attempt. SPCX stock is down nearly 23% since its debut, with retail sentiment on Stocktwits ‘bearish’ at the time of writing. For updates and corrections, email newsroom[at]stocktwits[dot]com. Shares of Sellas Life Sciences (SLS) jumped 3% overnight late Monday as retail traders bet that the final acute myeloid leukemia (AML) readout could turn this week’s Fox appearance into a launchpad for Big Pharma interest. SLS stock surged 12% on Friday to close at $13.19, capping a 3% weekly gain. The speculation is related to Sellas’ Phase 3 Regal trial of galinpepimut-S (GPS) in AML. The study is nearing the 80th event required to trigger its final analysis. Retail sentiment on Stocktwits sllipped to ‘neutral’ from ‘bullish’ levels a week ago amid a 12% rise in 24-hour message volumes. However, watchers for the stock have risen nearly 5% in a month. One trader called CEO Angelos Stergiou’s media strategy a “masterclass in forcing a Big Pharma decision,” saying that the period between the 80th event and topline data could trap short sellers. “We aren't waiting for a buyout—we’re manufacturing the conditions that make a bidding war inevitable,” the user said. Another investor expects Sellas to announce the topline results around Stergiou’s Fox appearance, while projecting a surge in the stock and a bidding war.  A third user said Stergiou had spent more than five years protecting Regal and would not risk the program for “30 minutes of television fame,” adding: “The timeline is compressed because the destination is set.” Other traders predicted that Stergiou would discuss the company’s two flagship drugs and the path to topline data. Several named Johnson & Johnson, Merck, Pfizer, AbbVie, Eli Lilly, and Bristol Myers as possible bidders. “One thing is for sure, JnJ will be watching Fox News,” another user said, citing LinkedIn activity. Stergiou said on LinkedIn last week that he would return to Fox & Friends after a recent discussion with host Brian Kilmeade about the future of AI-powered cancer vaccines. He said that the segment’s date and time were still being finalized, adding that the discussion would cover Sellas’ clinical programs and efforts to advance more personalized cancer care through GPS and SLS009 (the company’s second clinical-stage drug candidate). Meanwhile, retail takeover speculation has intensified as the market value swelled from about $73 million at the start of 2024 to more than $1.5 billion by mid-2026, with Regal nearing completion. Investors have pointed to Stergiou’s previous references to “strategic partners,” changes to executive change-of-control benefits and the potential commercial value of GPS and SLS009 (the second drug). Regal is a Phase 3 study evaluating GPS in AML patients who have entered a second complete remission. The trial had reached 78 of the 80 events required to trigger its final analysis. Sellas has said that the study would be considered successful if GPS extends median overall survival to 12.6 months, compared with eight months for best available therapy. Stergiou previously said the company would announce the 80th event and then enter a formal quiet period until topline results are available. He has also pushed back against claims that the slower event rate necessarily means patients in the control arm are surviving longer. Since Sellas remains blinded, neither the company nor investors know which arm is responsible for the slower accumulation of events. The CEO has also rejected calls to stop the trial at 78 events, saying, “Events are our statistical currency,” and warning that an early halt could create regulatory concerns and timing bias. Shares of Trump Media & Technology Group Corp. (DJT) are on track to clock their best month since April 2025 amid a series of fresh catalysts for the media company. DJT stock is up nearly 25% in July so far, posting four consecutive days in the green last week. The surge comes largely amid the July 4 launch of the Trump Accounts mobile app, which gives millions of Americans easy access to manage their children's investments. The app, which has been built by Bank of New York Mellon (BNY) and Robinhood Markets Inc. (HOOD), is available on Apple and Google app stores. As per the latest data, over 6.5 million families have signed up, including more than 1.5 million children eligible for the $1,000 pilot contribution from the government. The president’s media company also made a series of other announcements that boosted sentiment. Earlier this month, the company said it is on track to complete its planned merger with TAE Technologies by the fourth quarter of 2026 or earlier, while abandoning plans to spin off TMTG's media assets. The combined company's board said that it will evaluate future strategic options after the deal closes. Last week, the company unveiled plans to launch a paid service to provide customers real-time access to Truth Social posts from major accounts, including U.S. President Donald Trump’s, although it did not explicitly mention the president. In a statement last Thursday, DJT said that it will launch Truth API, a new business-to-business data feed, expected to become available to institutional customers from Aug. 1. Over the weekend, Trump Media also said it had settled all legal claims with former CEO Patrick Orlando, and ARC Global Investments II LLC in a confidential settlement agreement. The dispute primarily revolved around control of the merger, share allocation and allegations that Trump Media improperly accessed ARC Global's confidential files during the de-SPAC merger. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around DJT stock was ‘neutral’ at the time of writing amid ‘high’ message volumes. One user said, “$DJT double digits tomorrow. Mark my post.” Shares of the company were trading around $9.61 at the time of writing. For updates and corrections, email newsroom[at]stocktwits[dot]com. NYSE Composite drew fresh attention on Wednesday as the integrated energy major featured prominently in coverage of a firmer crude backdrop, a widely reported multi-year commitment to expand Venezuelan crude production, and continued discussion of the company's planned capital budget for the coming year. Trading in the name unfolded against a market where energy sat squarely in focus, even as broad US indices came under pressure from rising Treasury yields and renewed inflation concern. The combination of a headline-grabbing overseas expansion and a steady spending framework kept Chevron among the more closely watched energy majors during the session. The integrated oil and gas segment spans exploration, production, refining, chemicals, and marketing, and Chevron ranks among the largest operators spanning that full chain. Firms of this scale tend to move with the rhythm of crude and natural gas pricing, refining margins, and the cost of capital that funds long-cycle projects. During the current stretch, crude prices firmed on reports of shipping disruption tied to the Strait of Hormuz, lifting sentiment across the group. At the same time, elevated bond yields raised the discount applied to distant cash flows, tempering enthusiasm for capital-intensive names. Chevron sits at the intersection of those forces, with a diversified asset base that spreads exposure across geographies and product streams. That breadth has historically helped the company absorb swings in any single region, though it also ties performance to the wider commodity cycle that governs the entire sector. Chevron operates upstream assets across the Permian Basin, the Gulf of Mexico, Kazakhstan, Australia, and a growing roster of international positions, alongside downstream refining and a substantial chemicals joint venture. The Permian remains a central engine, prized for its flexibility and relatively short cycle times, which allow output to be dialed up or moderated as pricing shifts. Management has emphasised capital discipline, directing spending toward assets that generate cash efficiently while restraining the pace of expansion elsewhere. The company's integrated structure means refining and chemicals can cushion periods of softer crude, since those units often benefit from lower feedstock costs. Chevron's operational focus in recent reporting centred on wringing efficiency from existing acreage and advancing a handful of large projects that are meant to sustain production over a multi-year horizon, a stance that fits the broader industry move toward measured growth rather than aggressive drilling. The most prominent recent development involved a widely reported plan to channel substantial capital into Venezuela over the coming years, aimed at roughly doubling crude production the company draws from that country. Coverage framed the commitment as a notable re-engagement with a region that carries both resource depth and a complicated operating history. Separately, Chevron was reported to be advancing partnership discussions tied to Vietnamese energy demand, part of a wider push to widen its international footprint. Reporting also noted efforts to expand the gas portfolio through positions in Argentina and the Mediterranean. Each of these threads points to a company willing to pursue selective growth abroad even as it holds spending discipline at home, a balance that featured heavily in how commentators described the name during the session. Across the wider energy complex, movement among oil and gas stocks reflected the pull between firm crude pricing and the pressure that higher borrowing costs placed on capital-heavy producers, a tension that shaped trading sentiment through the session. Chevron has outlined a spending framework for the coming year that keeps capital within a defined band, signalling continuity rather than a sharp acceleration. The approach reflects a preference across the major producers to fund distributions and steady project execution while avoiding the boom-and-bust spending patterns that marked earlier cycles. By anchoring the budget within a stated range, management aims to give the market a clear read on how cash generated at prevailing prices is likely to be deployed. The framework covers upstream development, downstream maintenance, and lower-carbon initiatives, and it sits alongside the company's stated aim of sustaining its dividend, long a defining feature of the name. Observers noted that a disciplined budget can steady sentiment when crude swings, since it limits the degree to which spending balloons during price spikes and contracts during downturns. Trading unfolded within a market where rising Treasury yields, firm inflation readings, and expectations of further central-bank action weighed on richly valued corners of the market, particularly technology. Energy, by contrast, drew support from firmer crude, creating a rotation dynamic that favoured producers on some sessions. For a name like Chevron, the environment cut both ways: stronger crude lifted the revenue backdrop, while higher discount rates pressured the present value of long-dated projects. The push and pull left the stock sensitive to each fresh data point on prices, yields, and geopolitics. Commentators described the setup as one where macro forces mattered as much as company-specific news, a reminder that even a diversified major remains tethered to the broader financial climate that governs how capital flows into and out of the energy complex. Across the wider industry, executives voiced concern about tightening global fuel supply, with some warning of strain in refined products even as crude drew geopolitical support. Shipping disruption near key chokepoints added a premium to seaborne barrels, sharpening focus on producers with flexible output. The period also saw continued discussion of how majors balance traditional hydrocarbon development against lower-carbon commitments, an ongoing theme that shapes capital allocation across the group. Chevron featured in this conversation given its scale and its stated aim of growing both conventional production and select lower-carbon lines. Chevron's scale, dividend history, and index membership make it a reference point for how the energy majors are faring within the S&P 500. When crude firms and yields climb at once, the name often becomes a lens through which the market reads the tug-of-war between commodity strength and financing pressure. title: CVX vs. TTE: Which Energy Major Has the Stronger LNG Growth Story? - The Globe and Mail
content: Chevron CorporationCVX and TotalEnergies SE TTE are two major integrated energy companies with significant oil and natural gas operations. Both are benefiting from a supportive commodity-price environment, but their LNG strategies provide an interesting basis for comparison. Chevron is expanding its natural gas and LNG portfolio while benefiting from strong production growth following the Hess acquisition. TotalEnergies, meanwhile, already has a large global LNG business and is pursuing additional projects to expand its position across the LNG value chain. With energy security becoming increasingly important and global LNG demand continuing to grow, investors may be wondering which energy major offers the stronger combination of growth, valuation and earnings momentum. Let's dive deep and closely compare the fundamentals of both stocks to determine which one is a better investment now. Chevron delivered a strong second quarter, with earnings of $12.1 billion and adjusted earnings of $12 billion. Worldwide production increased 20% year over year to 4.07 million barrels of oil equivalent per day, while U.S. production reached a record level. The company also achieved $3 billion in annualized structural cost savings and $1.5 billion in annualized Hess-related synergies. The Hess acquisition has significantly strengthened Chevron's production profile, particularly through its interest in Guyana's Stabroek Block. Management expects production to continue growing, supported by Guyana, the Permian Basin, Kazakhstan and other projects. Chevron is also becoming more aggressive in LNG. The company expects to have about 20 million metric tons per annum (Mtpa) of LNG supply capacity, including 16 Mtpa of net gas production from its projects and 4 Mtpa of contracted U.S. Gulf Coast supply. Chevron is also evaluating additional opportunities in Argentina, the Eastern Mediterranean, Australia and Africa. The push reflects growing demand for diversified and reliable gas supplies. TotalEnergies brings a more established LNG platform to the comparison. The company sold 44 million tons of LNG in 2025 and describes itself as the world's third-largest LNG player. It expects LNG volumes from equity production and long-term third-party purchases to increase 50% between 2025 and 2030. The company is continuing to add projects to its portfolio. In July, TotalEnergies shipped the first LNG cargo from the ECA LNG project in Mexico and will offtake 1.7 million tons per year for 20 years once commercial operations begin. TotalEnergies also approved development of the Cronos gas field in Cyprus, with production expected to start in 2028. The project is designed to supply European markets through existing LNG infrastructure in Egypt. These developments give TotalEnergies substantial exposure to the LNG growth opportunity, while its integrated model also provides exposure to oil, refining, trading and electricity. Valuation is one area where the two stocks show a notable difference. Based on the data, Chevron trades at a forward P/E of 13.35X, compared with 8.46X for TotalEnergies. Chevron's higher multiple reflects its strong production growth, Hess-related synergies and high-quality upstream assets. However, TotalEnergies offers investors exposure to a substantial LNG business at a considerably lower earnings multiple. The valuation gap is also consistent with recent peer data showing TotalEnergies trading below Chevron on forward earnings multiples. TotalEnergies has outperformed Chevron over the past year. The chart shows TTE's share price gaining 48.8%, compared with a 30.7% increase for CVX. TotalEnergies' performance reflects investor interest in its integrated energy model, LNG exposure and capital returns. TTE reported second-quarter adjusted net income of $6 billion and cash flow of $9.8 billion, while its gearing ratio declined to 13%. Chevron, meanwhile, continues to benefit from strong operating momentum. Its second-quarter cash flow from operations reached $22.6 billion, compared with $8.6 billion in the year-ago quarter. Over the past 60 days, the Zacks Consensus Estimate trend for CVX's third-quarter 2026 earnings has increased 18.98%, while the fourth-quarter estimate has risen 20.83%. Meanwhile, the consensus estimates for fiscal 2026 and 2027 have increased 11.55% and 12.16%, respectively. In comparison, the Zacks Consensus Estimate for TTE's third-quarter 2026 earnings has increased 9.72%, while the fourth-quarter estimate has risen 31.12%. The consensus estimates for fiscal 2026 and 2027 have increased 6.69% and 11.74%, respectively. The stronger upward revisions for Chevron coincide with its recent production growth, cost reductions and improved earnings performance. TotalEnergies has also recorded positive estimate revisions across all four periods, although the increases were smaller in three of the four periods. Both energy majors have compelling LNG growth stories. Chevron offers rapidly growing production, Hess-related synergies and an expanding LNG portfolio. TotalEnergies brings a much larger established LNG business, a broader global portfolio and a substantially lower valuation. The data also show stronger one-year share-price performance for TotalEnergies, while Chevron has delivered more pronounced upward earnings estimate revisions. TotalEnergies carries a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy), while Chevron has a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold). Based on the combination of its lower valuation, established LNG platform, stronger recent share performance and Zacks Rank, TTE holds the edge in this face-off.You can see the complete list of today’s Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here. title: Chevron (CVX) Stock Gains Momentum as CFO Signals Prolonged High Oil Prices - Blockonomi
content: Shares of Chevron experienced a 1.4% uptick on Wednesday, peaking at $207.00 during intraday trading before closing around $205.21. The session witnessed more than 8.2 million shares exchanged. Trading volume registered a 23% decline compared to the typical daily average of approximately 10.7 million shares. The previous trading day concluded with shares at $202.41. Analyst sentiment toward the energy behemoth remains predominantly positive. The Street consensus shows a “Moderate Buy” rating alongside a mean price objective of $211.35. Among the more optimistic assessments, Piper Sandler elevated its price target from $207.00 to $243.00 earlier this month. Additional recent coverage from Jefferies and Sanford C. Bernstein included buy ratings and market perform designations respectively. During a Tuesday evening appearance at a WSJ Leadership Institute dinner held in New York, Chevron’s CFO Eimear Bonner outlined expectations for continued elevated energy prices. She cited ongoing disruptions to shipping routes through the Strait of Hormuz and limited refining capacity as key factors. Brent crude experienced a 1% decline on Tuesday, settling just below the $100 per barrel threshold. Bonner emphasized that Chevron’s strategic priority centers on optimizing supply output while maintaining operational reliability across its refining operations. The CFO also provided updates on Chevron’s Venezuelan operations. Earlier this month, the company announced a $7 billion commitment to develop the country’s oil reserves through three separate joint ventures spanning five years. However, Bonner tempered expectations by noting Venezuela won’t contribute significantly to new supply in the immediate future. Looking ahead, Chevron has outlined plans for an approximately 50% surge in exploration capital expenditures for next year. This aggressive drilling campaign aims to bolster future production capacity and reserve levels. Additionally, Greece’s energy ministry confirmed that Chevron will commence seismic research activities in offshore exploration blocks before the year concludes, expanding the company’s geographical exploration footprint. Chevron delivered better-than-anticipated results in its most recent quarterly earnings release on July 31st. The oil giant reported earnings per share of $6.06, surpassing the consensus forecast of $5.55. Quarterly revenue totaled $67.20 billion, significantly exceeding analyst projections of $62.72 billion. This represented a substantial 57.4% year-over-year increase compared to the corresponding quarter. The company maintains a quarterly dividend distribution of $1.78 per share, translating to an annualized yield of 3.5%. The current payout ratio registers at 68.26%. On a less favorable note, corporate insiders have divested more than 1.15 million shares valued at approximately $225.9 million during the past three months. Notable transactions included substantial sales by CEO Michael Wirth and board member John Hess. Regulatory uncertainty also looms with the proposed Diesel Price Reduction Act of 2026, which could impose temporary limitations on diesel exports when domestic prices exceed $5 per gallon. The legislation currently has minimal congressional support. Chevron’s current market capitalization approaches $405.45 billion, accompanied by a price-to-earnings ratio of 19.68. Technical indicators show the 50-day moving average positioned at $200.25, while the 200-day moving average rests at $191.97. American oil companies also got a sentiment boost after Trump said last week that China had agreed to buy crude oil from the U.S. following the recently-concluded bilateral summit in Beijing. Shares of the United States Oil Fund (USO) rose 2%, while Exxon Mobil Corp. (XOM) climbed 0.7%, Conoco Phillips (COP) gained 0.9%, Chevron Corp. (CVX) was up 0.45%, and Venture Global Inc. TIME IS OF THE ESSENCE!" The comments come shortly after the president’s visit to China, a country with close ties to Tehran. Investors were hoping for a significant breakthrough after the visit. Brent crude futures expiring in July were up about 1.81%, trading at around $111.30 a barrel, while WTI crude futures expiring in June were 2.18% higher, at $107.72 a barrel at the time of writing. The conflict between the U.S. and Iran has stayed high despite a ceasefire announced in early April. The U.S. has continued to blockade Iranian ports, even as the critical Strait of Hormuz has stayed shut since the conflict began. Meanwhile, reports have said that Iran has called the U.S. blockade an “act of war,” threatening further damage to countries around the world if the blockade continued. Mohsen Rezaei, a member of Tehran’s Expediency Council and former IRGC commander, has reportedly said that the Iranian military is ready for further confrontation. “We advise the US military to end the siege before the Sea of Oman becomes your graveyard,” Rezaei reportedly said. “It is America that must prove itself now,” he said. “Our armed forces have their finger on the trigger, and, at the same time, diplomacy continues.” Meanwhile, China agreed to buy crude oil from the U.S. last week. “They have an insatiable appetite for energy, and we have unlimited energy,” Trump said in an interview with Fox News, adding that “we’re doing twice as much oil and gas, as they are,” referring to the U.S. producing more oil and gas than Saudi Arabia and Russia combined. Convex Finance is a decentralized finance (DeFi) protocol built to enhance rewards for holders of staked Curve Finance tokens (CRV). Convex Finance was designed to fill the gap for CRV token holders who did not meet the criteria required to enjoy the 2.5x rewards boost offered to tiered investors in exchange for liquidity locked on the Curve.fi platform. Holders of staked tokens on the platform receive Vote-Escrowed CRV (veCRV) tokens, which are governance tokens needed to vote on proposed developments to the network. CRV holders must lock and stake their tokens to receive veCRV tokens that allow them to participate in the governance system. CRV can be locked for this purpose for up to four years, and CRV holders receive veCRV on a 1:1 basis for each CRV they stake. Convex Finance enhances this rewards system by making the rewards available to all holders of staked CRV. Those who would otherwise not hold enough staked CRV are able to receive the Curve Finance rewards boost by investing in liquidity pools available on the Convex Finance platform. Convex Finance users benefit not only from staking CRV but also other digital assets that can be integrated into the ERC-20 Curve.fi platform.
